notes: Reference renderer. Use to validate palette output before targeting other platforms.
Full init block support. Good secondary validation target.

advisory: GitHub strips %%{init}%% blocks. Diagrams render with GitHub's forced theme. Theming via init block has no effect. Use the themeVariables JSON export with mermaid.initialize() at the application level if you control the site config.
notes: Standard GitHub README files and issue comments cannot be themed.

advisory: GitLab strips %%{init}%% blocks similarly to GitHub. Platform-enforced theme applies.
notes: Same restrictions as GitHub for standard Markdown files.

advisory: Notion does not support Mermaid themeVariables or %%{init}%% blocks. Diagrams render with Notion's default Mermaid appearance. No workaround is available within Notion's editor. Consider exporting as a styled SVG image from mermaid.live and embedding the image instead.
notes: No theming of any kind is possible for Notion-hosted diagrams.
Best themeVariables support among Markdown host applications. Test with both light and dark vault themes.

advisory: Confluence Mermaid support depends on the installed plugin. Official Atlassian Mermaid plugin v1.3+ respects %%{init}%% blocks. Older or third-party plugins may not. Check your plugin version and test in your Confluence instance.
notes: Plugin version is the critical variable.
Requires Mermaid Preview extension or equivalent. Current extension versions fully respect init blocks.
Configure via themeConfig.mermaid.options.themeVariables in docusaurus.config.js. Inline init blocks also work in MDX.
Configure via markdown.mermaidOptions in vitepress.config.ts. Inline init blocks respected.
Use --configFile for site-wide theming or embed %%{init}%% inline. Ideal for CI/CD diagram generation pipelines.
Depends on Backstage Mermaid plugin version. Recent versions support themeVariables via plugin config. Init blocks may not be respected.
